_readme: Content only a developer may change.
This file is the single source. tools/check_locked.py reads it and enforces
it after a push, where the person publishing cannot skip it. The admin panel
reads it in the browser to render these fields read-only and to refuse a
publish that touches them. Duplicating the list in JavaScript would put two
copies in the repo that can drift apart, which hard rule 9 in CLAUDE.md
forbids. figures.json is shared for the same reason.
TWO KINDS OF LOCK
paths   a location in data/site-data.json. Everything under it is locked.
tokens  a phrase, wherever it appears. Locked because the CLAIM is
regulated, not the field that happens to hold it today.
A token lock fires when the CLAIM changes, not when the string holding it
changes. Both sides of an edit are matched and the matched text compared,
so adding, removing or altering a claim is refused while a typo fix
elsewhere in the same paragraph is not. Counts are compared too, so a
second identical claim still fires.
It used to fire whenever either side merely CONTAINED the token. Eleven of
the fifteen post bodies mention one of these claims somewhere, so that
locked eleven post bodies rather than the four the path list names, and
fixing a typo in one needed a developer. A lock that makes ordinary work
impossible is not obeyed, it is routed around, and then none of the locks
are consulted at all.
EVERY REFUSAL MUST TEACH. Someone blocked from writing 'ISO 3632 certified'
who is not told the approved wording will write 'internationally certified
quality' instead, which is a vaguer false claim rather than a precise one.
That outcome is worse than the one the lock prevents. Token locks therefore
carry an 'instead' giving the approved phrasing.
PATTERNS MUST BE PORTABLE between Python re and JavaScript RegExp, because
both run them. Stay inside the common subset. tools/check_locked.py compiles
every pattern on startup and rejects Python-only syntax.
dev: A developer changes this through a pull request.
unchanged: Nothing was published and the live site is unchanged.

paths.why: It promises a full refund plus the cost of the test within 90 days. It was reconciled against the returns policy on window, remedy and coverage, and the two contradicted each other until that was fixed.

paths.what: a policy page (terms, returns, shipping or privacy)
paths.why: Regulatory text. The returns window, the remedy and the FSSAI registration line all live here. A policy slug also moves a live web address.
These carry the crocin figure, the ISO category, the testing laboratory and its NABL accreditation number. They are claims about a measured result, not descriptions.
It is printed in the footer of every page as an official registration. A wrong number is a regulatory problem, not a typo.

paths.what: the 'Why We Do Not Make Health Claims' article
paths.why: It quotes FSSAI regulation 10(1) and UAE.S/FDS 2333 clause 11.1.4 verbatim. Both quotations were checked against the source documents.

paths.what: the 'How to Read a Saffron Lab Report' article
paths.why: It states the 190 against 200 crocin disagreement and deliberately refuses to resolve it in our favour.

paths.what: the 'What Origin Actually Tells You' article
paths.why: It cites two published studies and the Spanish PDO specification, each verified against the source.

paths.what: the 'How to Test Saffron Purity at Home' article
paths.why: The purity checker's reasoning is anchored to sentences in this body. Editing it breaks those anchors and tools/check_checker.py will fail.
Every option is anchored to a published sentence. The three outcomes are deliberately not a score.

tokens.why: The approved wording is "lab tested to ISO 3632 Category I", never the bare grade and never "certified". Category I is a band, not a score, and the site says so in several places.
tokens.instead: The approved wording is "lab tested to ISO 3632 Category I", never the bare grade and never "certified". Write your copy without the testing claim and ask a developer to add that phrase. Do NOT reach for a vaguer substitute such as "internationally certified" or "premium certified quality": a vague claim we cannot evidence is worse than a precise one, not safer.

tokens.why: "Category I" is a laboratory result for a specific lot, not a marketing adjective.
tokens.instead: Ask a developer. The approved phrasing is "lab tested to ISO 3632 Category I".

tokens.why: NABL accreditation belongs to the testing laboratory, not to us. The accreditation number TC-9209 identifies a real body.
tokens.instead: Ask a developer. Write the copy without the accreditation claim and they will add the approved wording.

tokens.why: FSSAI registration is a legal status with a number attached.
tokens.instead: Ask a developer. Write the copy without the registration claim and they will add the approved wording.

tokens.why: It identifies the accredited testing body and must match the certificate.
tokens.instead: Ask a developer. The number must match the certificate, so it is never typed from memory.
